objective: Enumerate every count of zero this lab has published as a finding and determine, for each, whether a positive control was run and reported beside it, on the grounds that a zero is the one result where an instrument that worked and an instrument that was never pointed anywhere produce identical output
rationale: The lab's highest-priority defect class is the sweep that silently returns nothing, and the response to it was a sanctioned helper that names its frame and filter and is tested against a planted file inside an ignored path. That helper landed, and sixteen published sweeps were re-run under it with four moved and three marked unframed. What has NOT been done is the complementary question, and it is the sharper one: the population at risk is not sweeps, it is ZEROS. Every conclusion of the form nothing was found is, considered as evidence, indistinguishable from a search that failed to run, and no amount of framing fixes that on its own; only a positive control does. The lab already produces zeros that carry real weight. Zero tracked files reference any wave machinery, which is the whole basis of a capability gap map. Zero of 257 reordering requests carry a readback, which is the basis of a defect filing and of an 8 core-minute arm. Zero dead levers on one case, which is the basis of a clean verdict. Some of those DID report controls and the audit that produced them says so; the point of this item is that nobody knows the proportion, and a proportion is what turns a good habit into a closed defect class. THE NULL, AND IT IS NOT FITTED: the population is derived mechanically from the corpus by a textual rule fixed and written down BEFORE any record is inspected, so the set of zeros is not chosen by whoever wants a particular answer. THE IDENTITY TEST, owner rule W dash 2. Could the gated quantity be derived by construction from its own inputs? The quantity is, per published zero, whether a control appears in the same record or its cited evidence. That is a property of the record's text and history, independent of the zero itself, so it is not an identity. But this item carries a self-application that it must not dodge: THE CENSUS IS ITSELF A SWEEP, AND IT CAN ITSELF RETURN A SILENT ZERO. It therefore runs under the sanctioned helper, plants its own positive control inside an ignored path, and reports the control's recovery before it reports any count. A census of silent zeros that returned a silent zero would be the funniest possible failure in this lab and it is guarded rather than joked about.
gate: ZERO COMPUTE. The rule that defines the population is written and committed BEFORE the first record is opened, and the commit is cited in the result. Then per zero, a three-valued classification: CONTROLLED if a positive control appears in the record or in the evidence it cites, with the control's own result stated; UNCONTROLLED if no control exists anywhere; INHERITED if a control exists in the canon but does not travel with the number, which is the transmission-loss shape the external referent audit already identified as this corpus's actual problem. The headline is the three counts and the frame, never a verdict. THEN THE ONE THAT DECIDES SOMETHING: take the uncontrolled zeros, order them by how much rests on each, and re-derive the top three under the sanctioned helper with a planted control. FAIL, meaning the class is not closed, if any re-derivation returns a different number than the published zero. PASS, meaning the helper's landing genuinely closed the class at corpus scale, if every re-derivation reproduces its published zero with its control recovered. NO VERDICT for any zero whose original frame cannot be reconstructed, which is the unframed disposition the earlier sweep re-run already uses. STANDING CONSTRAINT ON THE COUNT ITSELF: this shell's recursive search honours ignore files and sees roughly a quarter of the tree, so every count reported here names its frame or it is not reported.
cost_basis: ZERO solver compute. Scored in agent tool calls: forecast 60, in the upper half of this lab's measured build-and-verify band of 33 to 72, because the item writes a rule, runs a framed corpus sweep, classifies by hand against three categories and then re-derives three findings with planted controls. Actual counted from the executing agent's transcript. Stated honestly: the classification step is the part most likely to overrun, because the earlier absolutes checker measured its own false positive rate at 74 percent on a hand-labelled sample and the labelling is what cost the time there.
expected_knowledge_gain: THE DISCRIMINATING OUTCOME, and it is a whole class rather than an instance. If a re-derived published zero comes back different, then the sanctioned helper's landing did not close the highest-priority defect class, every conclusion resting on a zero is suspect, and the lab learns that from one cheap pass instead of from an embarrassment later. If all three re-derive cleanly with controls recovered, the class can be argued closed at corpus scale on evidence rather than on the fact that a helper was written, and the proportion of uncontrolled zeros becomes a number the lab can watch. The proportion itself changes nothing on its own and is reported rather than gated on.
hard_criterion_note: Starts no flow case. Reads records and re-runs searches over the corpus.
citations: The docket's first and highest-priority defect class, the sanctioned sweep helper with its four named frames, three verdicts and its test asserting it sees a planted file inside an ignored path, and the re-run of sixteen published sweeps with four moved and three unframed
The dead-lever audit, for the zero-tracked-files wave finding and for the zero readbacks against 257 reordering requests
The external referent audit, for the transmission-loss classification this item borrows as its third category
The absolutes checker's measured false positive rate of 74 percent on a hand-labelled sample, cited as the cost anchor for the classification step rather than as a result

launch_prompt: Published-zero census. ZERO COMPUTE. Step 1: write and COMMIT the textual rule that defines a published zero before opening a single record, and cite that commit in the result. Step 2: run the population sweep through the sanctioned helper with a planted positive control inside an ignored path; report the control's recovery BEFORE any count, and state the frame of the count. Step 3: classify each zero as controlled, uncontrolled or inherited. Step 4: re-derive the top three uncontrolled zeros with planted controls and apply the three-valued verdict. Do not repair anything you find; classification only, and file residuals to the docket with fresh append-only identifiers. Record your own tool call count.
